keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Mossi row). The Mossi states are drawn as one block: the page gives no founding year and dates the Ouagadougou dynasty by Oubri ("around 1050 to 1090 CE"); oral tradition spans the 11th to 15th centuries. No area on the page. The core is the provinces round Tenkodogo and Ouagadougou (proxies).

ledger.note: c. 1050: the Mossi kingdoms of Tenkodogo and Ouagadougou. "Oubri, who ruled from around 1050 to 1090 CE, is often considered the founder of the Ouagadougou dynasty"; Ouédraogo, son of Princess Yennenga, "built Tenkodogo". The page notes the oral traditions date the story "somewhere between the 11th and 15th centuries", so 1050 is a confidence-1 anchor.

wars.name: Mossi raids on Timbuktu and Walata
wars.outcome: "In the 15th century, the Mossi took over Timbuktu and sacked Walata"; historians debate whether the attackers were Yennenga's descendants. No change of frontier.
wars.note: The page gives no year (the 14th-century date sometimes given is not on it).

wars.name: Askia Muhammad's jihad against the Mossi
wars.outcome: Askia Mohammad I "waged a holy war against the Mossi kingdoms in 1497"; the Mossi resisted, and after the Saadi conquest of Songhai in 1591 "the Mossi states reestablished their independence".
wars.note: No territory is described as taken.

notes:
Mossi Kingdoms, additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Pages: Mossi Kingdoms, History of Burkina Faso; the Yatenga page (the province, not the kingdom) and a Kingdom of Ouagadougou page (not found) gave nothing and are not cited.

One block for several independent kingdoms (Tenkodogo, Ouagadougou, Yatenga, Fada N'Gourma, Boussouma, Zondoma, Rizim): the pages give neither per-kingdom founding years nor outlines, so one dossier and one colour; a later gap-filler could split it. The dossier would need dynastic pages for Ouagadougou and Yatenga.

Weak points: (1) 1050 is the page's reign of Oubri, whose historicity is uncertain (oral tradition 11th-15th centuries); the start is a confidence-1 anchor. (2) No frontier or area; the shapes are provinces round the cities (proxies). (3) End: infobox "conquest by France in 1896" versus the History of Burkina Faso page "resistance ended only with the capture of Ouagadougou in 1901". (4) The 1894 British treaty of protection (Ferguson) is on the Mossi page; no territorial effect. (5) The Mossi page puts the Mossi under Songhai pressure only as a jihad (1497) and "reestablished their independence" after 1591; Songhai's own dossier dates a Mossi invasion in 1483.
Gazetteer: Tenkodogo, Ouahigouya, Fada N'Gourma (places) and Mossi plateau (region) are not in the gazetteer.
